RATE ADJUSTMENT MECHANISM PROCEDURE 
KEDNY and KEDLI will implement a Rate Adjustment Mechanism (“RAM”) beginning 
in Rate Year One.  The purpose of the RAM is to consolidate certain deferral account 
balances into a single surcharge/credit for recovery from or refund to customers.   
1.0 
Eligible Deferral Accounts 
The deferral balances as of March 31st of each year for the following accounts will be 
eligible for inclusion in the RAM.   
i.
Property Taxes1;
ii.
Energy Affordability Program (“EAP”)2; and
iii.
Exogenous Costs (but excluding costs related to pending Pipeline and Hazardous
Materials Safety Administration rulemakings discussed in subsection (i) of the
Exogenous Costs deferral, as such costs are subject to a separate recovery
mechanism discussed in that section).3
(Collectively, the “Eligible Deferral Accounts”).  
For accounting purposes, the Eligible Deferral Accounts will continue to be maintained 
and accounted for in their respective accounts in the general ledger.  As of March 31st of 
each year, the deferral balances in the Eligible Deferral Accounts will be reclassified and 
combined into a new general ledger account.  The net deferral balance in this account will 
be reflected in the RAM for surcharge or sur-credit each Rate Year subject to the annual 
cap listed in Section 2.0 below.   
In future proceedings, KEDNY and KEDLI may propose different deferral accounts for 
inclusion in in the RAM.  
2.0 
Annual RAM Recovery/Return Limits 
In Rate Year One, the RAM will include the deferral balances for the Eligible Deferral 
Accounts as of March 31, 2024, and be recovered/credited during the 12-month period July 
1, 2024 through June 30, 2025.   
The RAM is subject to an annual cap of 2.00 percent of KEDNY and KEDLI’s respective 
actual operating revenues for the prior calendar year (operating revenues as reported in the 
Public Service Commission (“PSC”) Annual Report, which excludes ESCO commodity 
revenues) and be recovered/credited during the collection period July 1 through June 30 of 
each Rate Year.   
1 See Section IV.8.15 of the Joint Proposal.  
2 See Section IV.8.1.2 of the Joint Proposal. 
3 See Section IV.8.1.3 of the Joint Proposal. 
Case 23-G-0225 
Appendix 3 
Schedule 12.1 
Page 4 of 5


--- Page 323 ---
3.0 
RAM Allocation 
The annual recovery/credit amounts reflected in the RAM will be allocated to the service 
classifications based on the following allocators: Property Taxes will be based on the 
General Tax allocator (Plant Based) and EAP will be based on the Total Revenue allocator. 
If there are Exogenous Costs to be recovered through the RAM, the appropriate allocator 
will be determined based on the nature of the costs to be recovered.  
4.0 
RAM Compliance Filing and Review Process 
In Rate Year One, KEDNY and KEDLI will file a statement surcharge before the effective 
date setting forth the amount of the RAM surcharge/credit and including the calculations. 
Beginning in Rate Year Two, by June 1st of each year, KEDNY and KEDLI will make a 
compliance filing with the Commission.   The filing will include the deferral balances to 
be recovered/refunded, allocation of amounts to be recovered/refunded from/to each 
service classification, and the per therm unit rate to be recovered/refunded during the 
collection period.  By June 15th of each year, the Companies will convene an informational 
meeting either in person or via teleconference of interested parties to these proceedings to 
review the Companies’ calculation of the RAM.  
In the event Staff or any interested party to these proceedings objects to the calculation of 
the RAM, Staff or such party shall notify the Companies and the parties in writing.  The 
Companies will respond in writing addressing the objection.  If Staff or other such party 
believes its concerns were not fully addressed by the Companies’ response, Staff or such 
party may submit written comments to the Commission. 
In the event of a dispute regarding the calculation of the annual RAM, the parties will use 
their best efforts to resolve the dispute within 120 calendar days of the Companies’ 
response. The parties agree to utilize the Commission’s dispute resolution process to 
resolve any contested matters.  If the parties are unable to resolve any remaining 
differences, the parties agree to present such differences to the Commission for resolution. 
RAM amounts will be subject to true-up and reconciliation, including carrying costs. 
The implementation of the RAM shall not limit Staff’s right to audit the deferred costs 
included by each Company in their respective RAMs.
